newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht stronger late, interbank rate drops.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht stronger late, interbank rate drops.

text.p: The baht strenghtened further against the dollar in late trade on Wednesday on U.S. unit's weakness abroad and sentiment toward the currency improved, dealers said.
The baht was stronger to 25.998/26.008 to the dollar in late trade from 26.010/26.020 earlier and 26.025/26.030 late on Tuesday, they added.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.98 per dollar against 25.99 on Tuesday.
"The baht was stronger following the dollar's fall abroad. But some dollar buying help cap the U.S. unit's weakness against the baht," one dealer at a foreign bank said.
The dealer said some players viewed the dollar's recent weakness as a buying opportunity on expectations it could possibly rebound later.
The rising confidence in the baht followed a firm Bank of Thailand's statement on Tuesday ruling out devaluation, dealers said.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was down further to 14.50/15.50 satangs per dollar late compared with 15.50/16.50 in the morning.
The overnight interbank rate fell to 11.00-11.50 percent late from 12.00-12.50 in the morning on steadily rising liquidity, dealers said.
